question: Can reversible, content-dependent index permutations expose enough latent low-rank structure in pretrained LLM weights and KV caches to improve tensor-network compression after permutation metadata, sign bits, reconstruction quality, and inference cost are all considered?

key_findings.claim: Reordering tensor entries can change the singular spectrum even though independent row and column permutations cannot; the useful case is an axis-coupled permutation whose ordering on one index depends on another index.
key_findings.evidence: The 2-by-2 example changes singular values from (3,1) to (sqrt(10),0) by j -> j xor i, while Proposition D.2 proves that independent left and right permutation matrices preserve every singular value. The appendix therefore identifies row-dependent, CNOT-like index maps as the relevant mechanism.

key_findings.claim: Full, row-wise, grouped, and sequential sorting substantially reduce low-rank reconstruction error on the displayed LLM weight matrices, with the non-full variants reported as more than ten times better than unsorted SVD at comparable rank.
key_findings.evidence: The Qwen3, Gemma3, and Phi-3.5 v/o-projection plots show near-rank-one behavior under full sorting and consistently lower error under lower-metadata orderings; the appendix states that row, group-size-64, and sequential-axis sorting remain over ten times lower-error than no sorting across the tested matrices.

anchors.section: C, Rank reduction with tensor sorting

key_findings.claim: The formal rank argument is much narrower than the pretrained-model claim: it applies to sorted i.i.d. samples, and its attempted extension beyond that setting is explicitly heuristic.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 2.1 gives an entrywise O_p(L^-1/2) approximation by a sum of three rank-one matrices for globally sorted i.i.d. uniforms, and Lemma D.1 gives relative-Frobenius rank-one convergence for row-sorted i.i.d. rows under density and quantile assumptions. Appendix D.2 admits that orthogonally mixed variables are not jointly independent and that marginal CLT convergence does not imply joint uniformity.

key_findings.claim: The auxiliary mean/product reduction proposition is not correct as written and its proof contradicts its stated variance.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition D.3 defines X_i,j as uniform on [-1,1] and Y/Z from |X_i,j|^p, but Equations 48 and 50 condition on the raw X_i,j and use X_i,j rather than |X_i,j|^p; for a negative conditioned value, the stated mean of the non-negative product Z would even be negative. The proof then calls the transformed variable Beta(1/p,0), although the displayed density is Beta(1/p,1), and Equations 60-61 use (M-1)/M where the variance of an M-term mean requires (M-1)/M^2 and where Equation 49 itself has M^2.

key_findings.claim: The finite-field permutation appendix overstates its algebraic coverage.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix M incorrectly expands gcd as 'greatest common multiple' rather than greatest common divisor and says a Galois field can realize permutations for arbitrary n. Finite fields exist only at prime-power cardinalities, so the proposed finite-field interpolation does not directly cover an arbitrary index size without an additional embedding or product construction.

key_findings.claim: EinSort is not a single decomposition but a search space that wraps a tensor network in a reversible permutation and optionally adds nonlinear scoring, slice-shared ordering, non-negative tensorization, and gauge-fixed cores.
key_findings.evidence: The method is T_pi,theta[X] = pi^-1[T_theta[pi[X]]]. The implemented heuristic folds a tensor, scores absolute p-th powers, reduces selected slice axes, shares an argsort over the remaining axes, optionally stores one sign bit per entry, and applies LU block-identity gauge fixing to reduce redundant core parameters.

key_findings.claim: Permutation storage is a first-order part of the compression problem and makes unrestricted sorting noncompetitive as a representation.
key_findings.evidence: A full permutation of a 1024-by-1024 tensor is estimated at about 18.6-19 bits per entry, already exceeding FP16 storage. Slice sharing lowers examples to about 0.4 bits per entry for a 32^4 tensor and, in the reported KV-cache configurations, to 1.44 bits for Qwen3, 3.14 bits for Gemma3, and 0.35 bits for Phi-3.5; non-negative tensorization adds another sign bit.

key_findings.claim: The plotted compression rates are not demonstrated to be end-to-end rates that include permutation indices and optional sign bits.
key_findings.evidence: The paper quotes permutation and sign overhead separately from the compression-rate axes and benchmark tables, but it never gives a total-byte accounting that combines tensor cores, gauge metadata, permutation payload, sign payload, and implementation padding. Consequently the reconstruction and task curves cannot by themselves establish the net memory ratio.

key_findings.claim: At 50% KV-cache compression on Qwen3-1.7B, the strongest reported design choice is product-reduced, power-mapped, non-negative tensorization with gauge fixing, reaching 33.17 perplexity versus 60.0 for regular SVD.
key_findings.evidence: Table 4 reports 33.17 for pow.nn plus gauge fixing with product reduction, compared with 36.29 without gauge fixing and 50.84 for the best linear-with-gauge product reduction; its caption states regular unsorted SVD has 60.0 perplexity.

key_findings.claim: The best reconstruction topology in the main KV-cache comparison is also the least practical in the supplied runtime implementation.
key_findings.evidence: CP has the best Table 2 perplexities at 90% and 80% compression (26.88 and 27.99), but Table 3 retains only 3.3% of baseline CPU throughput and 3.7% of baseline GPU throughput. SVD retains 78.7%/79.6%, while TT retains about 62%, so quality and wall-clock ranking disagree sharply.

key_findings.claim: The paper's operation-count examples do not translate into demonstrated inference acceleration.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B estimates that contraction-order optimization can cut a TT reconstruction by nearly three orders of magnitude and a direct weight-activation contraction by more than five, but the measured KV-cache decoder loses 20%-97% throughput depending on topology. The authors state that the implementation validates compression rather than optimized kernels and later list missing compatible high-performance CUDA kernels as a limitation.

key_findings.claim: The paper mixes two materially different empirical applications: the main language-model figures compress runtime KV states, whereas the multimodal and robotics appendices compress model weights.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 partitions WikiText-2 into 64-token prefill and 64-token decode segments and tensorizes the KV cache. By contrast, the TextVQA experiments compress linear weights in the Qwen3-VL language backbone, and the LIBERO experiments compress attention and MLP linear weights in VLA backbones.

key_findings.claim: Weight-compressed VLAs retain nearly all reported LIBERO success at settings where the low-rank baselines collapse.
key_findings.evidence: Across 800 rollouts per model, EinSort averages 92.38% for X-VLA at compression rate 0.1 versus 93.63% original and 2.63%-26.25% for baselines; 97.13% for pi-0.5 at rate 0.4 versus 97.75% original and 4.25%-57.38% for baselines; and 97.75% for VLA-JEPA at rate 0.8 versus 97.50% original and 0%-59.75% for baselines. The paper notes that apparent gains over the original fall within Wilson intervals.

key_findings.claim: The reproducibility appendix identifies architectures, datasets, licenses, and most software versions, but does not supply the run-level information needed to reproduce uncertainty or total deployed compression.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 8-15 enumerate Qwen, Gemma, Phi, Qwen3-VL, X-VLA, pi-0.5, and VLA-JEPA dimensions and model IDs; the dataset appendix gives split sizes and sources; and Appendix U pins most libraries. Across these pages there are still no random seeds, repeated-run counts for the LLM/VLM curves, serialized core/permutation/sign artifacts, or one byte-accurate compression manifest.

key_findings.claim: The direct permutation-enhanced tensor-decomposition antecedent is TQCompressor, so the broad idea of improving neural-network tensor factorization with permutations predates EinSort.
key_findings.evidence: TQCompressor is cited in the bibliography and discussed only in Appendix D.4, where EinSort argues that its independent row/column permutations cannot change singular values. The remaining novelty is therefore the axis-dependent content sorting, its rank analyses, shared-permutation memory tradeoff, and the broader KV/weight evaluation rather than permutation-assisted tensor compression itself.

key_findings.claim: The paper's dismissal of TQCompressor does not follow from its independent-permutation proposition.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition D.2 proves only that independent row and column permutations preserve an ordinary matrix's singular values and matrix rank. TQCompressor instead optimizes a permutation-enhanced Kronecker decomposition, so unchanged SVD rank does not establish unchanged Kronecker approximation error or tensor-network bond requirements. The proposition supports EinSort's axis-coupling motivation but not the broader claim that TQCompressor 'should have no benefit' for tensor ranks.

anchors.section: D.4, Proposition D.2 and TQCompressor inference

key_findings.claim: The method selection burden is large and mostly tuned per model rather than explained by a general rule.
key_findings.evidence: Qwen3 prefers a product reduction and a power exponent near one in one setting, while Phi-3.5 prefers an exponent around 0.4 with non-negative tensorization and above two without it. The framework also searches folding, slice modes, reduction, topology, rank, nonlinear map, and gauge choice; the authors list finding the best configuration as a limitation.

method.core_idea: Permute tensor entries with a reversible, content-dependent, axis-coupled ordering before low-rank tensor decomposition, then invert the permutation after reconstruction so that the factorizer sees a smoother and lower-effective-rank arrangement.
method.mechanism: Fold a weight or KV tensor, compute an element score through a nonlinear map, reduce selected slice axes to share one ordering over many entries, argsort the score on the remaining axes, optionally factorize absolute values while storing signs, decompose the sorted tensor with SVD/TT/TR/CP/Tucker cores, gauge-fix redundant core parameters, reconstruct, invert the ordering, and restore signs. The central tradeoff is reconstruction rank versus permutation, sign, search, and execution overhead.
assumptions: The rank lemmas assume i.i.d. samples and, for the general row-sort result, a continuous distribution with density bounded away from zero and a square-integrable quantile function.
The heuristic extension through orthogonal mixing assumes marginal Gaussianization is useful despite dependence between transformed coordinates.
Practical slice-shared score reductions are assumed to preserve enough elementwise ordering information to expose low-rank structure.
Reported compression benefits assume permutation and sign metadata can be stored and applied cheaply enough; the plots do not provide a unified end-to-end byte count.
Task accuracy is assumed to be preserved by post-training tensor reconstruction, sometimes with activation calibration, without retraining the base model.

techniques.role: Reorders entries across tensor modes so the ordering on one axis depends on other indices and can change effective rank.
Shares a score-derived permutation across slices to trade sorting fidelity for lower metadata cost.
Factorizes magnitude after a power map while retaining one sign bit per entry for approximate inversion.
Chooses among SVD, TT, TR, CP, Tucker, folding schemes, ranks, and contraction orders.
Converts cores to block-identity form to remove redundant junction parameters.
Extends sorted decomposition to calibrated weight-space objectives used for VLM and VLA weight compression.

evaluations.setting: First-layer projection weights from Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B, Gemma3-4B, and Phi-3.5-mini
evaluations.metric: Squared reconstruction error versus retained rank
evaluations.result: Full sorting approaches near-rank-one reconstruction; row, group, and sequential sorting are reported as more than ten times lower-error than no sorting while using less permutation metadata.
evaluations.baseline: Unsorted truncated SVD and full sorting

evaluations.metric: Perplexity under mapping, reduction, gauge, and sign ablations
evaluations.result: The best table entry is 33.17 perplexity for product-reduced power/non-negative tensorization with gauge fixing, versus 60.0 for regular SVD; configurations vary widely from 33.17 to above 80.
evaluations.baseline: Regular SVD, full-sort SVD, and alternative score reductions

evaluations.setting: Qwen3-0.6B KV-cache topology and decoding runtime
evaluations.metric: Perplexity at 80%-90% compression and throughput relative to uncompressed decoding
evaluations.result: CP gives the best reported perplexity (26.88/27.99) but only 3.3% CPU and 3.7% GPU throughput; SVD retains about 79% and TT about 62% throughput.
evaluations.baseline: SVD, TT, TR, CP, and Tucker decompositions

evaluations.metric: Math-answer accuracy and visual-question-answering accuracy across KV or weight compression ratios
evaluations.result: EinSort curves remain above regular SVD for GSM8K and preserve substantially more TextVQA accuracy at aggressive weight compression, but the figures do not report repeated-run uncertainty.
evaluations.baseline: Plain SVD for KV cache; plain SVD, ASVD, SVD-LLM, and LatentLLM for weights

evaluations.setting: LIBERO robot manipulation with X-VLA, pi-0.5, and VLA-JEPA, 800 rollouts per model
evaluations.metric: Success rate across Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long suites with Wilson 95% intervals
evaluations.result: EinSort averages 92.38%, 97.13%, and 97.75% at the respective reported rates, close to 93.63%, 97.75%, and 97.50% uncompressed and far above the tested low-rank baselines.
evaluations.baseline: Original model, plain SVD, ASVD, SVD-LLM, and LatentLLM

evaluations.metric: Entrywise or relative-Frobenius approximation by low-rank sorted matrices
evaluations.result: Global sorted uniforms are approximated entrywise by rank at most three with O_p(L^-1/2) residuals; row-wise sorted i.i.d. matrices converge relatively to a rank-one quantile template at O_p(N^-1/2).
evaluations.baseline: Unordered i.i.d. matrices and independent axis permutations

limitations: Author-stated: selecting topology, folding, index ordering, rank, nonlinear score, slice reduction, and gauge is not straightforward.

Author-stated: large tensor factorizations are computationally challenging, permutation memory is difficult to reduce, and compatible optimized CUDA kernels for contraction plus reordering are unavailable.
Author-stated: the broader-distribution theory after random projection is heuristic because transformed coordinates are dependent and marginal CLT convergence does not yield joint uniformity.
Reviewer inference: the asymptotic i.i.d. order-statistic results do not establish low-rank exposure for correlated pretrained weights, KV states, or the actual sliced-score heuristic.
Reviewer inference: compression-rate plots and tables do not explicitly include a unified accounting of core parameters, permutation codes, sign bits, gauge metadata, and alignment/padding.
Reviewer inference: most LLM/VLM task curves do not report seeds or run-to-run uncertainty; only the LIBERO tables provide confidence intervals.
Reviewer inference: KV-cache accuracy, VLM/VLA weight accuracy, and runtime are evaluated in different regimes, so no single experiment establishes an end-to-end memory-quality-latency frontier.

Reviewer-identified: Proposition D.3 mixes raw uniform variables with their absolute-power transforms, names an invalid Beta(1/p,0) law, and drops a factor of M in the proof's conditional-mean variance, so its reduction-scaling statement is not established as written.

Reviewer-identified: Proposition D.2 establishes invariance only for ordinary matrix singular values/rank; it does not justify dismissing a permutation-enhanced Kronecker decomposition's approximation benefit.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix M incorrectly defines gcd and invokes a finite field for arbitrary n even though finite fields have prime-power size.
failure_modes: If the score-reduced shared permutation misorders entries, the transformed tensor can remain high rank while still paying index overhead.
Full or fine-grained sorting can cost as many or more bits than the original FP16 tensor, eliminating net compression.
Non-negative tensorization adds a dense sign payload and its clamp-plus-inverse-power reconstruction can introduce distortion not reflected in a rank-only analysis.
A topology such as CP can win perplexity yet lose almost all decoding throughput under available kernels.
Hyperparameters that work for Qwen3 need not transfer to Phi, Gemma, multimodal, or dynamic KV distributions.
Content-dependent cache permutations may add latency or irregular memory access that contraction FLOP counts do not predict.
Calibration-aware weight compression can fail under distribution shift when the 64 calibration samples or episodes do not represent deployment inputs.
reusable_insights: Treat index layout as an optimization variable in low-rank compression, but include the exact permutation code in every rate calculation.
Independent row and column reorderings cannot change singular values; rank-changing permutations must couple tensor axes.
Separate approximation quality, serialized size, and measured wall-clock speed because their rankings can reverse.
A shared permutation across slices is a general rate-distortion control knob for metadata-heavy transforms.
Gauge fixing can remove genuine parameter redundancy after factorization and should be accounted for separately from approximation rank.
Use direct task metrics after tensor reconstruction because low Frobenius error alone does not predict language, vision, or control behavior.
open_questions: Can a theorem cover correlated pretrained tensors and the actual sliced product/mean score rather than globally sorted i.i.d. samples?
What is the Pareto-optimal quality after entropy-coding the exact permutations and signs, including decode-time workspace and padding?
Can fused GPU kernels make axis-coupled reordering plus direct tensor contraction faster than dense or low-rank baselines at the same total bytes?
Can permutations be learned under a differentiable objective that includes serialized metadata and measured latency without an intractable search?
How stable are learned or calibrated orderings across prompts, sequence positions, batches, and distribution shift?
Does the apparent LIBERO robustness persist across seeds, real-robot evaluation, and compression ratios defined by total deployed storage?

competitive_landscape.title: TQCompressor: improving tensor decomposition methods in neural networks via permutations
competitive_landscape.difference: TQCompressor already improves neural-network Kronecker tensor decomposition through permutations and demonstrates compressed GPT-2. EinSort's narrower advance is content-derived, axis-dependent sorting with shared-permutation tradeoffs, explicit order-statistic analyses, and KV/VLM/VLA evaluations.

competitive_landscape.title: TensorGPT: Efficient Compression of Large Language Models based on Tensor-Train Decomposition
competitive_landscape.difference: TensorGPT applies training-free tensor-train decomposition to GPT embedding layers and reports device latency; EinSort changes the entry ordering before arbitrary tensor-network decomposition and targets weights and KV caches beyond embeddings.

competitive_landscape.title: ASVD: Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Compressing Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: ASVD rescales weights with activation statistics and covers both weight and KV-cache low-rank compression without permutation metadata; EinSort uses index ordering and can optionally wrap the same activation-aware preconditioning.

competitive_landscape.title: SVD-LLM: Truncation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: SVD-LLM uses truncation-aware whitening and sequential low-rank updates with no learned index transform; EinSort tries to expose a more compressible spectrum before factorization and reports larger gains on its VLM/VLA tests.

competitive_landscape.title: Palu: Compressing KV-Cache with Low-Rank Projection
competitive_landscape.difference: Palu compresses hidden dimensions through medium-grained low-rank projections and supplies fused GPU kernels with measured speedups; EinSort reports better reconstruction through sorting but currently slows decoding and lacks fused reordering kernels.

competitive_landscape.title: ReCalKV: Low-Rank KV Cache Compression via Head Reordering and Offline Calibration
competitive_landscape.difference: ReCalKV reorders structurally similar key heads and calibrates values before grouped SVD, avoiding per-cache content permutations; EinSort uses finer axis-coupled element ordering and pays explicit permutation storage for each compressed tensor.

competitive_landscape.title: AA-SVD : Anchored and Adaptive SVD for Large Language Model Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: AA-SVD explicitly models upstream distribution shift and refines transformer blocks to compensate accumulated error; EinSort does not model cross-layer error in its core method and instead searches for a permutation that reduces local factorization rank.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Brain Decomposition for Accurate LLM Low-Rank Approximation
competitive_landscape.difference: OBD-LLM derives bidirectional whitening from a Kronecker-factored Hessian and gives a closed-form weight approximation; EinSort is largely objective-agnostic but introduces a discrete ordering search and separate permutation/sign costs.

competitive_landscape.title: KV-CoRE: Benchmarking Data-Dependent Low-Rank Compressibility of KV-Caches in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: KV-CoRE measures optimal SVD compressibility layer by layer across domains and languages and relates normalized effective rank to downstream degradation. It does not reorder entries or provide a deployed codec, but it supplies the data-dependent rank audit missing from EinSort's short-context, model-specific sorting studies.

competitive_landscape.title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: VarRate allocates a nonzero token-specific low-rank budget from query salience and reports matched-memory LongBench results without content-permutation codes. EinSort instead rearranges tensor entries before factorization, evaluates 64-token prefill plus 64-token decode in its main KV setup, and has not shown the same long-context rate-quality comparison.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first EinSort framework that augments tensor-network einsum decompositions with reversible adaptive index sorting, provides theory that sorting can reduce effective tensor rank, and improves LLM weight and KV-cache compression across language, vision-language, and robot-control evaluations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The strongest new evidence is the axis-coupled ordering analysis, slice-shared permutation construction, large reconstruction-error reductions, model-dependent score ablations, and broad downstream tables. Lemma 2.1 and Lemma D.1 support an idealized ordering effect but do not cover the deployed heuristic; Proposition D.3's separate reduction analysis contains variable, distribution, and variance inconsistencies.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Permutation-enhanced neural tensor decomposition is not new because TQCompressor is a direct 2024 antecedent, and tensorized LLM, activation-aware SVD, reordered KV, and error-aware low-rank methods are established. Proposition D.2 does not erase that antecedent because SVD-rank invariance does not imply invariance of Kronecker-decomposition quality. The defensible novelty is the specific axis-dependent sorted-einsum construction, its shared-score/sign/gauge design space, the two idealized order-statistic lemmas, and the unusually broad KV/VLM/VLA evaluation. Claims of practical compression remain provisional until total serialized bits and optimized latency are reported together.

verification.passage_check: Independently re-read all 38 pages of arXiv:2606.08565v1 and rechecked every finding and anchor against Figures 1-17, Tables 1-15, the weight/KV/VLM/VLA protocols, runtime table, memory estimates, pseudocode, Lemma 2.1, Lemma D.1, Propositions D.2-D.3, gauge derivations, and Appendices A-U. Numeric table transcriptions and the negative CP runtime result agree with the PDF. The second pass added concrete corrections for Proposition D.3's raw-versus-power variable mismatch, invalid Beta label, and missing variance factor; Proposition D.2's overextension to TQCompressor; and Appendix M's gcd/finite-field errors.
verification.competitor_check: Independently checked titles, methods, relevance, and current official arXiv histories for ten primary records: 2401.16367v1, 2307.00526v2, 2312.05821v5, 2403.07378v5, 2407.21118v2, 2505.24357v3, 2604.02119v1, 2604.00821v1, 2602.05929v2, and post-target VarRate 2607.15498v1. Every item now carries a full arXiv ID-plus-version pin and the target itself is excluded.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification covered every page of the exact cached arXiv:2606.08565v1 PDF, including all proofs, tables, figures, implementation pseudocode, negative runtime results, speculative extensions, benefits/limitations, and multimodal/robotics appendices through page 38. The local PDF/text hashes and page count remain exactly index-derived. Confidence is highest for the displayed reconstruction/task tables, independent row/column SVD invariance, and explicit permutation-bit examples; it remains lower for transfer from i.i.d. sorting theory to pretrained tensors, Proposition D.3's flawed reduction derivation, and net compression because total cores/permutations/signs/workspace are never jointly counted. Ten current primary competitors were independently checked on official arXiv records on 2026-08-23, including a post-target long-context KV competitor.
